title.narrative: Public perception of the effectiveness of the peace process

description.narrative: Public perception of the effectiveness of the peace process

comment.narrative: Public perception of the effectiveness of the peace process in this action will be measured by comparing results from the first and second Consultations. As this peace process is new there will be no baseline perception of its effectiveness. The first Consultation is likely to provide learning on public perception of previous peace processes perhaps including those at national level such as the Juba Peace Agreement whose architects have been politically sidelined by the events of October 25th 2021.

Public perception of the effectiveness of the peace process in this action will be measured by comparing results from the first and second Consultations. The target for the second Consultation is that people report that local conflicts are resolved to mutual benefit and that there is an improvement to their experience of peace.

189 respondents at 9 townhall meetings evaluations of 206 Advisory Group members from 16 localities Peace Committee members Womens Peace Ambassadors and 104 participants in peace conferences reported that they now have a better sense of the needs of the other side and are willing to work together to resolve conflicts to mutual benefit.
